_comment: Government reforms, Paradox style: tiers unlocked in order as reform progress accrues (base 2 a month, more with stability and legitimacy); each tier offers a choice. requires_government: the government law options the reform is open to.

reforms.name: Hereditary kingship
reforms.description: The crown passes from father to son; no one disputes it.

reforms.name: Council of elders
reforms.description: The great men sit with the king and share his counsel.

reforms.name: The priest-king
reforms.description: The king is the god's own servant, and his word the god's.

reforms.name: Assembly of citizens
reforms.description: The free men of the city decide in assembly.

reforms.name: Royal governors
reforms.description: Men of the king's choosing rule each province.

reforms.name: Tributary lords
reforms.description: The local lords keep their lands and send their levies.

reforms.name: Temple provinces
reforms.description: The temples hold and govern whole districts.

reforms.name: Royal monopolies
reforms.description: The crown alone trades in the richest goods.

reforms.name: Tax in kind
reforms.description: Grain and cattle, measured and stored.

reforms.name: The granary law
reforms.description: Stores against famine keep the realm steady.

reforms.name: The standing guard
reforms.description: A permanent force at the king's side.

reforms.name: Chariot nobility
reforms.description: The great families keep the chariots.

reforms.name: Levy of the land
reforms.description: Every village sends its men when the king calls.

reforms.name: A written code
reforms.description: The law set in stone for all to see.

reforms.name: Royal judges
reforms.description: The king's men judge in every town.

reforms.name: Sacred law
reforms.description: The gods' commandments are the realm's law.

reforms.name: King of kings
reforms.description: Lesser kings do homage; the neighbours fear less a lord who already has many.

reforms.name: League of cities
reforms.description: The cities of the realm trade as one.
